_comment: Enforcement-boundary labels are not always Lean definition names. This maps a label to the definition the arm reaches, so scripts/check_live_arm_per_core_routing.py can walk it. Missing alias = hard failure, never a silent skip. Every entry here is VERIFIED against the live dispatch arm in SeLe4n/Kernel/API.lean (PR #861 review round 15): the gate rejects an alias the arm does not call, so a coincidental name match can no longer stand in for the real operation. Round 16: the verification now strips leading-dot constructor references before looking for the root, so an arm header (`| .schedContextUnbind =>`) or a decode guard (`decoded.syscallId = .schedContextUnbind`) can no longer stand in for a call — which is what let the schedContextUnbind label pass while the arm called the OnCore wrapper.
_alt_note: Round 20: a `<label>#alt` entry names the OTHER production root of a syscall that has two dispatch arms — the unchecked arm alongside the information-flow-checked one.  Both are walked.  Before this the arms were concatenated and only the mapped root was scanned, so a boot-pinned regression confined to the unchecked arm left the gate green.
_inert_note: A `<label>#inert` entry declares that one of this syscall's dispatch arms performs NO operation, so there is no body to walk for boot-pinned scheduler reads.  Declared rather than inferred, and VERIFIED by the gate (the arm must call nothing and must produce an error), so an edit that gives the arm a call turns the exemption back into a demand for a root.  `.declassify`'s unchecked arm is the first: there is no unchecked declassification, because 'unchecked' would mean 'every downgrade authorized', so `dispatchWithCap` fails closed with `.declassificationDenied` (dispatchWithCap_declassify_denied).
_audit_reader_note: PR #870 review: the enforcement-boundary label for the audit-trail read is now `auditReadFromCore` — the LIVE entry point the `.auditRead` arm calls — so no alias is needed and the routing walk audits the subject-resolution seam itself (the first cut labelled the inner query `auditReadWord`, which takes a caller-supplied reader domain; coverage tracking that helper would have stayed green had the live seam drifted onto the confused-clearance shape).  The drain's label was the live entry from the start.  Both audit syscalls' UNCHECKED arms are inert for the same reason the declassification's is: every value the reader returns is selected by the caller's clearance, which lives in the `LabelingContext` the unchecked path does not carry, so `dispatchWithCap` fails closed with `.illegalAuthority` (dispatchWithCap_auditRead_denied).
_declassify_signal_note: The data-carrying declassification's unchecked arm is inert for exactly the reason `.declassify`'s is, and one more.  Its authority is a policy at TWO hops, so an unchecked arm would mean 'every downgrade into this notification, and every onward delivery out of it, is authorized' — and the second half is sharper, because the ordinary checked `.notificationSignal` already gates notification -> receiver (the badge-leak closure at v0.31.73), so an unchecked declassifying variant would be strictly weaker than the syscall it wraps while carrying stronger authority.  `dispatchWithCap` fails closed with `.declassificationDenied` (dispatchWithCap_declassifySignal_denied).
